description: This repository watches Renovate, so it runs under the same rules it reports on. Anything configured here that the watchdog depends on is documented in README.md under 'What the watched repositories need'.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The security label is not decoration: the watchdog identifies a security pull request by this label plus Renovate authorship, and matching on the title instead produced nineteen false positives. A null minimumReleaseAge lets a fix for a known advisory bypass the cooldown, because a published advisory means the version is already being examined by everyone.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Regenerate the committed lockfile on a schedule so transitive dependencies pick up published fixes. An advisory against a package that no manifest names is never resolved until the lockfile itself is refreshed. The watchdog reports the absence of these commits, so turning this off here would leave it reporting its own repository forever.

packageRules.description: Group routine updates into one weekly pull request and merge it once Renovate observes the checks pass. One run a week rather than one per dependency, because Actions minutes on a private repository are finite.
Major updates require human review. The final private-repository grouping rules collect reviewed updates without changing this merge requirement.
Update the TypeScript compiler and the node type declarations together. Both are devDependencies used only for typechecking, and a mismatched pair fails the typecheck rather than anything at runtime.
The node version is stated in three places that must agree: engines, .nvmrc and the README. Renovate can move .nvmrc on its own, so it is held for review rather than merged into a disagreement.
Private repository: combine eligible automatic updates after package-specific rules to conserve Actions minutes. Keep existing review requirements unchanged.
Private repository: bundle review-required updates without enabling automerge. Keep majors separate from reviewed non-major updates so incompatible major upgrades do not block other reviewed fixes.
